name: abx-workspace
description: ABX protocol, SDK, CLI, and reference services.
//test-shard: `test:shard` exists for a CI matrix and is NOT wired into the workflow yet, on purpose.
Node's --test-shard partitions correctly (1440 tests split 479/426/535 across 3 shards), and
sharding is the right next lever because the dominant cost is CPU-BOUND tsx transpilation --
~0.35s per CLI spawn across 37 spawn-heavy files -- so extra runners add real cores, whereas
raising concurrency on one 2-core runner only time-slices the same two.
The blocker is merge GATING, not mechanics: `typescript` is the required status check. Matrixing
it renames the checks to `typescript (1/3)` etc, so the required check would never report again;
moving tests OUT of it would leave merges gated on a job that no longer runs them. Doing this
safely needs an aggregator job that keys off `needs.<shard>.result` with `if: always()`, plus a
branch-protection update -- a change to what can merge, which is the repo owner's call.
//test-concurrency: Node defaults test concurrency to availableParallelism()-1. A standard 2-core CI runner therefore
runs the suite EFFECTIVELY SEQUENTIALLY, which is why CI's test step took 518s of a 770s job while
the same suite finishes in ~50s on a 12-core dev machine. The work here is I/O-bound, not
CPU-bound: most of it is spawning the CLI as a subprocess (~0.35s of tsx transpile each) and
waiting on RPC. So concurrency can safely exceed the core count -- the cores are not the
constraint, the waiting is. MEASURED. Six spawn-heavy files: concurrency 1 = 57.0s vs 8 = 27.8s
(2.05x), same 101 tests. Full suite on a 12-core box: default(11) = 43.9s, 8 = 41.0s,
16 = 43.2s, 24 = 46.9s -- so 8 is also the FASTEST choice locally, not a cap that penalises a
strong machine; past ~16 oversubscription costs more than it buys.
Not raised further on purpose: every concurrent file may hold RPC calls open, and more parallel
requests against a public endpoint invites the 429s that have already cost us a sweep run.
The floor is the LONGEST single file (deploy-code.test.ts, ~37s locally) -- no concurrency beats that.

scripts.test: node --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=8 packages/sdk/test/*.test.ts packages/indexer/test/*.test.ts packages/storage-arweave/test/*.test.ts packages/storage/test/*.test.ts packages/token-api/test/*.test.ts packages/cli/test/*.test.ts packages/effects/test/*.test.ts
scripts.test:shard: node --import tsx --test --test-concurrency=4 --test-shard="$ABX_TEST_SHARD" packages/sdk/test/*.test.ts packages/indexer/test/*.test.ts packages/storage-arweave/test/*.test.ts packages/storage/test/*.test.ts packages/token-api/test/*.test.ts packages/cli/test/*.test.ts packages/effects/test/*.test.ts
